extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: A benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (i.e., IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA).
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets, including 9 math-targeted question answering datasets and 19 VQA datasets. In addition, three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were created. Examples were automatically filtered using heuristic rules and then manually labeled by expert annotators.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms and academic papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates (examples with numeric answers or containing quantity words). This yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples, which were then manually labeled by three expert annotators. Majority voting was utilized, and each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: All questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and further refined through a rigorous review process. Each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team to reach a consensus.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The initial independent annotation by three reviewers resulted in a high inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%. Among the newly collected 736 questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements, which were resolved through discussion. The human labeling of mathematical problems yielded a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields and expert annotators.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic rules for automatic selection of mathematical problems and automatic annotation for the labeling of mathematical reasoning from source dataset details.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is part of an ongoing research process. The creators are committed to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Facilitates the development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, such as solving complex problems in educational disciplines, helping analysts with logical queries about statistical data, and assisting in theorem proving and scientific discovery.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage may have gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. Annotations sourced from original data providers lack a unified format and structure due to the heterogeneity of these sources. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts, model development validation (testmini subset), and standard evaluation (test subset).
